A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the power-divergence statistic SD λ is asymptotically normal with mean and variance that depend on λ, and that the normal approximation is valid for increasing cells with fixed numbers of parameters.
, for increasing cells and large degrees of freedom, the asymptotic distribution of SD λ is normal with expectation and variance given by simple formulae.
for increasing cells, the asymptotic distributions for all SD λ's, including X 2, G 2 and the Cressie-Read statistics, are normal.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for the first time, we have shown that the power-divergence family of goodness-of-fit tests can be used for sparse data, and that the tests are applicable to large degrees of freedom, which is a common situation when the number of parameters to estimate increases with the sample size.
the asymptotic normal approximation to the power divergence test statistic is accurate for large sample sizes, regardless of the value of the parameter $\lambda$.
the normal approximation to the chi-square distribution is a good approximation when the number of degrees of freedom is large.
